title: H3060 (124th General Assembly): Concealed weapons permit

provenance.fetched_by: LegiScan bulk data (gun-policy Stage 5, South Carolina); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official South Carolina text (Introduced, 2020-12-09; official copy, https://www.scstatehouse.gov/sess124_2021-2022/prever/3060_20201209.htm (LegiScan doc 2220184))
provenance.note: Introduced text, Dec. 9, 2020. No votes. Struck: the old requirement that the other state run a background check and training course, the SLED reciprocity list, and 'the reciprocity requirements of' in item (2). New item (3) on permitless-carry state residents (needs photo ID) is not quoted for length; it is in the text.

operative_text:
Section 1 (Section 23-31-215(N)): (1) A valid permit or license to carry a concealable weapon, firearm, or handgun held by a resident of another state shall be honored by this State, provided that the person is a resident of the issuing state.
Section 1 (Section 23-31-215(N)): (2) Notwithstanding item (1), South Carolina shall automatically recognize concealed weapon permits issued by Georgia and North Carolina.
Section 1 (Section 23-31-215(N)): (4) The reciprocity provisions of this section shall not be construed to authorize a person to carry, in this State, any firearm or weapon other than a handgun. A person carrying a gun in this State pursuant to this section is subject to and must abide by the laws of South Carolina regarding concealable weapons.
Section 1 (Section 23-31-215(N)): (5) The Attorney General shall enter into a written agreement with another state if that state requires a written agreement in order to recognize permits to carry concealable weapons issued by this State.
